title: One certified solver for all five merge rules via a rule-parameterised interpretation
intent: Certify the pipeline's solver contract `certified_solver` once, for the single interpretation `TD_side_rule_Interp` parameterised by the `globals_rule` value `r`, so that all five merge rules (join, per-origin, warrow, warrow-per-origin and bounded narrowing) inherit the contract from one proof instead of each discharging it separately.

applicability.goal_shape: A locale or contract with several assumptions (here certified_solver, four assumptions), parameterised by a value that selects among finitely many concrete instances (globals_rule r, five constructors).
applicability.use_when: a family of instances shares one contract and differs only by a value; the contract's assumptions hold uniformly of the parameterised object, so one interpretation discharges them for every value at once.
applicability.avoid_when: the instances need different arguments for some assumption (the uniform interpretation does not close a case), or the parameter is a first-class choice that each proof must reason about separately rather than a value passed to one interpretation.

claims.claim: The main theorem td_certified_solver is declared in src/Abstract_Interpreter/Solver/Globals_Rule.thy at lines 157-165.
The parent site td_certified_solver is 9 lines long.
The authors state the move in the file's own comment: "a single interpretation takes the rule as a parameter, and every solver fact holds for all five at once."

The authors record that this one fact is reused: "`td_certified_solver` (`Globals_Rule`) discharges it for every `globals_rule`; the generated `<Domain>_Analyses.thy` registrations cite that one fact."

metrics.how_counted: parent_lines = lines 157-165 of the parent site; children = the four TD_side_rule_Interp facts cited in the glue; rule_constructors = constructors of globals_rule (lines 18-23 of Globals_Rule.thy)

consequences: The move replaces five per-rule interpretations with one: update_rule_update_global_of proves the update-rule obligations once for update_global_of r (by `cases r`, an exhaustiveness obligation over the five constructors, lines 142-146), the interpretation lifts that into the TD_side_upd_rule facts for every r, and td_certified_solver discharges certified_solver from them. The obligation it creates is exhaustiveness over the rule value: if a new globals_rule constructor is added, update_global_of and update_rule_update_global_of must be extended, but the solver-contract proof does not change. The failure mode is a non-uniform instance: if some rule needed a different argument for an assumption, the single interpretation would not close that case and per-rule proofs would be needed.
